citations.quote:
Adopt as physical assumptions of the relativistic particle model, on top of the
flat spacetime model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and the SI unit
conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], together with
the framework's idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks and ideal light
signals:

**(i) Mass and momentum.** Every massive classical particle of the model
carries a positive constant invariant mass parameter $m>0$ and has
four-momentum $P=mU$, where $U$ is the four-velocity of its future timelike
worldline ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]],
[[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]],
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]); $P$ is a vector of $V$
whose SI unit is kilogram metre per second. The formula is adopted only for
$m>0$; the case $m=0$ is not defined by it and is the separate premise
[[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]. In particular $\eta(P,P)=-m^2c^2$
is a consequence of the four-velocity normalisation, not a separate
assumption.

**(ii) Observer measurement identification.** Relative to a future unit
observer $n$, the model identifies the measured energy of the particle with
$E_n(P)$, its measured spatial momentum with $q_n(P)$, its kinetic energy with
$T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ and its rest energy with $mc^2$, where $E_n,q_n,T_n$ are
the quantities of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; the
units are the joule, kilogram metre per second and kilogram of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. This clause is a formulation
convention identifying mathematical quantities with the quantities the model
calls measured; it is not a measurement report and no experiment is claimed.

**(iii) Isolated collision balance.** An isolated collision is represented by
a mass-specified on-shell collision datum at an event, with finite nonempty
incoming and outgoing lists of the massive particles of (i) and/or the ideal
massless particles of [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]], and with
no external four-momentum transfer or omitted leg. The interaction is
idealized as confined to that event. The sum of the incoming four-momenta equals the sum of the
outgoing four-momenta, in the sense of the collision data of
[[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]]: the model adopts
$Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$ for such an isolated datum. No particular
collision is asserted to occur, and no mechanism, probability, cross section
or amplitude is supplied by this clause.

**(iv) Equation of motion for a stipulated force.** Put
$H_c^+:=\{U\in C^+:\eta(U,U)=-c^2\}$. A stipulated force law is a given
map $F:D\to V$ on a given subset $D\subseteq A\times H_c^+$,
with force components in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m/\mathrm s^2$. No regularity
away from the specified worldline is assumed. Along a given $C^2$ massive worldline
$x:I\to A$ with $(x(s),U(s))\in D$ for all $s\in I$, the model's particle
equation is $m\,dU/d\tau=F(x,U)$, with
$dU/d\tau$ the proper-time derivative of
[[def-sr-proper-time-derivative-and-four-force]], so that the stipulated $F$
is the four-force of the motion. A particular force law, and the existence,
uniqueness and domain of solutions of the resulting equation, are not adopted
here and belong to a separate model.

Empirical support for these assumptions is a nonlogical relation of the
framework, not a proof; the idealisations of point particles, ideal clocks,
ideal light signals and flat spacetime are inherited and travel to every
consumer of this premise.

Use the massive and null sectors as separately adopted in [[post-rpm-massive-test-particle-action]] and [[post-rpm-null-test-particle-action]]. For a massive body of constant mass $m>0$, its **mechanical four-momentum** is $P=mU$, where along an admissible $C^2$ future timelike trajectory $x:I\to M$, with $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval with nonempty interior and parameter $s$, put $T=dx/ds$, and $U:=cT/\sqrt{-g(T,T)}$ is its future tangent normalized by $g(U,U)=-c^2$. The clock convention in the massive-sector adoption gives $d\tau/ds=\sqrt{-g(T,T)}/c$, so $U=dx/d\tau$. In the null sector, the mechanical four-momentum is the separately specified nonzero future-null vector $P$ from the einbein formulation; no null proper time or $P=mU$ is defined.

At an event, for any observer $n$ of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]], define the spatial momentum and observer energy by

$$q_n(P):=P+g(P,n)n\in n^\perp,\qquad E_n(P):=-c\,g(P,n).$$

The projection identity and positive-definiteness of $n^\perp$ are supplied by [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. With SI units, $P$ has units kg m s$^{-1}$, $q_n$ has the same units, and $E_n$ has units joules. This definition is pointwise and does not assert conservation, positivity, or an energy interpretation for an arbitrary vector field that is not an observer.

Let $c > 0$ and let $(A,V,\eta,C^{+})$ be an oriented time-oriented affine
Minkowski space ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

**(a) Norm of the four-velocity.** Let $x : I \to A$ be a $C^{1}$ future
timelike worldline with four-velocity $U$
([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]). Then
$\eta(U(s),U(s)) = -c^{2}$ for every $s \in I$; equivalently the dimensionless
four-velocity $u = U/c$ satisfies $\eta(u,u) = -1$, and $U(s)$ is future
timelike. Thus the dimensionless four-velocity lies on the future unit
hyperboloid $\{v \in C^{+}:\eta(v,v)=-1\}$.

**(b) Orthogonality of the four-acceleration.** If $x$ is $C^{2}$ at $s$, then
$\eta(U(s),A(s)) = 0$: the four-acceleration has no component along the
four-velocity; if in addition $A(s) \ne 0$, then $A(s)$ is spacelike.

**(c) Rest space and projection.** Let $n \in V$ be future unit timelike,
$\eta(n,n) = -1$, and put $n^{\perp} := \{\,v \in V : \eta(n,v) = 0\,\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]). Then $n^{\perp}$ is a
3-dimensional linear subspace of $V$, the restriction of $\eta$ to $n^{\perp}$
is positive definite, and the map $h : V \to V$, $h(v) := v + \eta(n,v)\,n$, is
linear, idempotent with $h \circ h = h$, has image $n^{\perp}$ and kernel
$\operatorname{span}(n)$, satisfies $h(n) = 0$ and $\eta(n,h(v)) = 0$ for all
$v \in V$, and every $v \in V$ has the unique decomposition
$v = -\eta(n,v)\,n + h(v)$. Moreover $|w| := \sqrt{\eta(w,w)}$ defines a norm
on $n^{\perp}$.

**(d) Relative velocity and Lorentz factor.** Let $n$ and $u$ be future unit
timelike vectors, put $\gamma := -\eta(n,u)$ and $w := c\,h(u)/\gamma$. Then
$\gamma \ge 1$, $w$ lies in $n^{\perp}$,
$u = \gamma\,(n + w/c)$, $|w|^{2} = c^{2}(1-\gamma^{-2}) < c^{2}$,
$\gamma = (1-|w|^{2}/c^{2})^{-1/2}$, and $\gamma = 1$ if and only if $u = n$.
The vector $w$ is the velocity of a worldline with four-velocity $cu$ relative
to the observer $n$, and $\gamma$ is its Lorentz factor.

**(e) Coordinate form.** Let $(o;e_0,\dots,e_3)$ be an inertial frame and let
$y$ be a $C^{1}$ future timelike worldline whose inertial coordinates are
$t \mapsto (ct,r(t))$, with coordinate velocity $w(t) := r'(t)$ in
$\mathbb{R}^{3}$ and, when $y$ is $C^{2}$, coordinate acceleration
$a(t) := w'(t)$. Then $|w(t)| < c$, the four-velocity is
$U = \gamma_w\,(c,w)$ with $\gamma_w := (1-|w|^{2}/c^{2})^{-1/2}$, and the
four-acceleration is $A = \gamma_w\,\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(\gamma_w(c,w)\bigr)$, so
that

$$A^{0} = \gamma_w^{4}\,\frac{w \cdot a}{c}, \qquad A_{\mathrm{vec}} = \gamma_w^{2}\,a + \gamma_w^{4}\,\frac{(w \cdot a)\,w}{c^{2}} ;$$

consequently
$\eta(A,A) = \gamma_w^{4}|a|^{2} + \gamma_w^{6}(w \cdot a)^{2}/c^{2} \ge 0$,
with $\eta(A,A) = 0$ if and only if $a = 0$, and $\eta(U,A) = 0$. For the
observer $n = e_0$ of the chart, clauses (c) and (d) specialize to
$\gamma = \gamma_w$ and $w_{\mathrm{rel}} = (0,w)$ in the frame coordinates, identified with $w$ via the spatial basis.

**(f) Scope.** The statement is a theorem about the affine Minkowski model with
a fixed positive constant $c$; it asserts no clock reading and identifies no
physical four-velocity. No choice principle is used.

Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the $C^2$ subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are $C^2$ curves $x:I\to A$, with tangent defined by differentiating the displacement $x(s)-o$ for any fixed $o\in A$, lying in the selected future timelike or nonzero null cone of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]. The derivative is independent of $o$ because a change of origin adds a constant displacement. No affine-line or geodesic condition is imposed.

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** on a nonempty open set $U$ means a smooth ordered frame field $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ with $g(E_a,E_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ for $a,b=0,1,2,3$, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A tetrad is **future-directed** when additionally $E_0$ is future-directed everywhere: $g(E_0,N)<0$ in the curved case, or $E_0(p)\in C^+$ in the flat case with $g=\eta$. In flat spacetime this future-directed subclass is the tetrad-field convention of [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]]; the unqualified tetrad here retains the general GR convention. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), with orientation fixed as a positive ray of
the determinant line $\Lambda^4V$
([[def-determinant-line-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space]])
and with the corresponding class of positively oriented ordered bases of $V$
([[def-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space]]); by
[[prop-orientations-and-positive-basis-classes-agree-in-positive-dimension]] the
positive ray selects exactly one such class for $\dim V=4>0$.

An **inertial frame** of the model is a tuple $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ consisting
of an event $o\in A$ and an ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $V$ that is

1. **$\eta$-orthonormal**: $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ for all $a,b$ ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]]);
2. **future**: $e_0\in C^+$, i.e. $e_0$ is future timelike; and
3. **positively oriented**: the ordered basis lies in the positive-basis class
   selected by the fixed orientation.

The event $o$ is the **origin** of the frame and $e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ are its
**basis vectors**.

**Inertial charts.** For an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, define

$$E:\mathbb R^4\longrightarrow V,\qquad E(u):=\sum_{a=0}^3u^ae_a .$$

Then $E$ is a linear isomorphism ([[def-linear-isomorphism-and-invertible-linear-map]]):
it is linear by construction, and it is bijective because
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is an ordered basis, every $v\in V$ having exactly one
coordinate list $u$ with $v=\sum_au^ae_a$
([[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]). The **inertial
chart** of the frame is the map

$$x:A\longrightarrow\mathbb R^4,\qquad x(p):=E^{-1}(p-o),$$

and its values $x^a(p)$ are the **inertial coordinates of the event $p$** in the
frame. Since $E$ and $v\mapsto p+v$ are bijections, $x$ is a bijection
$A\to\mathbb R^4$; and $x(p)=0$ exactly when $p-o=0_V$, that is, exactly when
$p=o$.

**Transition law.** Let $(o';e'_0,e'_1,e'_2,e'_3)$ be another inertial frame
with chart $x'$, and let $M=(M^b_a)$ be the change-of-basis matrix defined by
$e'_a=\sum_bM^b_ae_b$, a $4\times4$ real matrix that is invertible because both
families are ordered bases. Then $E'(u)=\sum_au^ae'_a=E(Mu)$ for all
$u\in\mathbb R^4$, for the matrix-vector product $Mu$ in the coordinates of the
first frame, because $\sum_au^a\sum_bM^b_ae_b=\sum_b(\sum_aM^b_au^a)e_b$; hence
$E'=E\circ M$ and $E'^{-1}=M^{-1}\circ E^{-1}$, so for every event $p$,

$$x'(p)=M^{-1}\bigl(x(p)-x(o')\bigr)=M^{-1}x(p)-M^{-1}x(o') .$$

In particular the transition between two inertial charts is an affine map of
$\mathbb R^4$ with invertible linear part $M^{-1}$ and constant part
$-M^{-1}x(o')$, and it is a bijection of $\mathbb R^4$ with inverse
$u\mapsto Mu+x(o')$, which is the transition in the reverse direction.

**The inertial atlas.** The **inertial atlas** of the model is the family of
all inertial frames together with their inertial charts. Its charts are
available at every event by [[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]], which
supplies for every $o\in A$ an inertial frame with origin $o$; and any two of
its charts are related by the affine transition displayed above.

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space and let
$(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Put

$$S:=\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)=\{w\in V:\eta(e_0,w)=0\},$$

the equality holding because a vector $w=\sum_aw^ae_a$ satisfies
$\eta(e_0,w)=-w^0$ by $\eta$-orthonormality, so $\eta(e_0,w)=0$ exactly when
$w$ is a linear combination of $e_1,e_2,e_3$. In particular $S$ is the linear
subspace of $V$ spanned by the three spatial basis vectors of the frame, and
$V=S\oplus\operatorname{span}(e_0)$.

Let $\delta$ be the restriction of $\eta$ to $S$, i.e.
$\delta(w,z):=\eta(w,z)$ for $w,z\in S$. Writing $w=\sum_{i=1}^3w^ie_i$ and
$z=\sum_{i=1}^3z^ie_i$ and using $\eta(e_i,e_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for $i,j\ge1$, one
has

$$\delta(w,z)=w^1z^1+w^2z^2+w^3z^3,\qquad \delta(w,w)=(w^1)^2+(w^2)^2+(w^3)^2 .$$

Hence $\delta$ is a symmetric bilinear form on $S$ that is positive definite:
$\delta(w,w)\ge0$, with equality exactly for $w=0$ by uniqueness of coordinates
in the basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $S$
([[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]). Thus $\delta$
is an inner product on the real vector space $S$
([[def-inner-product-space]]); the induced function

$$\lvert w\rvert:=\sqrt{\delta(w,w)}=\bigl\lVert(w^1,w^2,w^3)\bigr\rVert_2$$

is the Euclidean norm of the coordinate vector of $w$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and it is a norm on $S$
([[cor-triangle-inequality-for-inner-product-norm]]). The ordered basis
$(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $S$ is $\delta$-orthonormal, and it is declared **positively
oriented** in $S$ by the convention that an ordered triple $(u_1,u_2,u_3)$ of
elements of $S$ is positively oriented when the ordered basis
$(e_0,u_1,u_2,u_3)$ of $V$ is positively oriented for the fixed orientation of
$V$. The pair $(S,\delta)$, together with this orientation and the frame's
basis, is the **Euclidean spatial structure of the inertial frame**
$(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$.

**Vector product.** For $w=\sum_{i=1}^3w^ie_i$ and $z=\sum_{i=1}^3z^ie_i$ in
$S$, define the **vector product** $w\times z$ to be the unique element of $S$
whose coordinates are

$$(w\times z)^1=w^2z^3-w^3z^2,\qquad (w\times z)^2=w^3z^1-w^1z^3,\qquad (w\times z)^3=w^1z^2-w^2z^1 .$$

This is well defined by uniqueness of coordinates in the basis
$(e_1,e_2,e_3)$. It is bilinear in $(w,z)$, alternating
($z\times w=-(w\times z)$ and $w\times w=0$), and it satisfies, for all
$w,z,y\in S$,

$$\delta(w\times z,y)=\det\begin{pmatrix}w^1&z^1&y^1\\ w^2&z^2&y^2\\ w^3&z^3&y^3\end{pmatrix},\qquad \lvert w\times z\rvert^2=\lvert w\rvert^2\lvert z\rvert^2-\delta(w,z)^2 .$$

The first identity is the expansion of the determinant along its columns, both
sides equalling $\sum_i(w\times z)^iy^i$; the second is Lagrange's identity,
obtained by expanding $\lvert w\times z\rvert^2+\delta(w,z)^2$ and comparing
termwise with $\lvert w\rvert^2\lvert z\rvert^2$ using
$\lvert w\rvert^2=\delta(w,w)$
([[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]]).

**Frame dependence.** The objects $S$, $\delta$, $\lvert\cdot\rvert$ and
$\times$ belong to the spatial three-space of the **named** inertial frame:
replacing the spatial basis by another $\delta$-orthonormal positively oriented
basis of $S$ transforms coordinates by an orientation-preserving orthogonal
matrix, under which $\delta$, the norm and the displayed identities are
unchanged, while a general change of inertial frame with a different time axis
$e_0$ changes $S$ itself and hence changes the domains of $\delta$ and $\times$.
The Lorentz form, the fixed orientation of $V$, and the time orientation $C^+$
are data of the model independent of the named inertial frame
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]). The Euclidean spatial structure instead
requires the choice of a time axis $e_0$; it is not an additional
frame-independent structure on the whole of $V$.

derivations.claim: By [A1] and [F2], $P=mU=(\gamma mc,\gamma m\mathbf v)$, and [F4] identifies these with the time and spatial components in the chosen frame. The definitions in [F1] give $E=\gamma mc^2$ and $\mathbf p=\gamma m\mathbf v$. Hence $E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=\gamma^2m^2c^4(1-|\mathbf v|^2/c^2)=m^2c^4$, and $\gamma m>0$ gives $E>0$.

Dividing the spatial identity $\mathbf p=\gamma m\mathbf v$ by $E=\gamma mc^2$ yields $\mathbf p/E=\mathbf v/c^2$, and therefore $\mathbf v=c^2\mathbf p/E$. The division is valid because $E>0$ by step 1.1.

Differentiating the mass shell of step 1.1 with respect to $t$ gives $2E\,dE/dt=2c^2\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf F$. Substituting $\mathbf p/E=\mathbf v/c^2$ from step 2.1 yields $dE/dt=\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf v$.

In inertial coordinates, $dP/dt=(c^{-1}dE/dt,\mathbf F)$, and [F2] gives $d/d\tau=(dt/d\tau)d/dt=\gamma\,d/dt$. Substituting the work identity of step 3.1 proves $K=\gamma(\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf v/c,\mathbf F)$. This is a kinematic identity, not a force law.

For the separate variable-mass ansatz, bilinearity and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ give $\eta(P,P)=m(\tau)^2\eta(U,U)=-m(\tau)^2c^2$. Since $m$ and $U$ are $C^1$, $P$ is differentiable and $K=dP/d\tau$ exists. Differentiating with respect to $\tau$ gives $2\eta(P,K)=-2m(dm/d\tau)c^2$, so $\eta(P,K)=-m(dm/d\tau)c^2$. No equation for $m$ was used.

citations.quote:
Throughout, $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ is the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski
model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and $c>0$.

**(a) Total four-momentum.** For a finite list $(P_1,\dots,P_N)$, $N\ge0$, of
vectors of $V$, define the **total four-momentum**
$P_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\sum_{i=1}^{N}P_i$ as the finite sum of
[[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]] in the additive group $(V,+)$ of
the vector space $V$; the empty sum is $0$. The sum uses the vectors $P_i$
alone: no event, no position and no simultaneity datum enters it, and the
order of the list does not affect $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ because addition in $V$
is commutative.

**(b) Invariant mass of the total.** If $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future timelike
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]), define the **invariant
mass** of the system and its **rest energy** by

$$M:=M(P_{\mathrm{tot}}):=\frac{\sqrt{-\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},P_{\mathrm{tot}})}}{c}>0$$

and its rest energy is $Mc^2$.

The square root is a real number because
$\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},P_{\mathrm{tot}})<0$ for a timelike vector, and it is
strictly positive, so $M>0$ ([[def-rational-power]]). If
$P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future null, set $M:=0$ and say that the system has no
rest frame. For $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ equal to zero, spacelike or past causal,
this convention defines no invariant mass.

**(c) Center-of-momentum frame.** A **center-of-momentum frame** of a nonzero
$P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) whose first vector satisfies

$$h_{e_0}(P_{\mathrm{tot}})=0,\qquad h_{e_0}(v):=v+\eta(v,e_0)e_0\quad(v\in V),$$

where the projection is defined on all of $V$; for a future causal total this
is $q_{e_0}(P_{\mathrm{tot}})=0$, meaning that its total spatial momentum
vanishes for the observer stationary in the frame
([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]). The condition is equivalent to
$P_{\mathrm{tot}}=-\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},e_0)e_0$, i.e. to
$P_{\mathrm{tot}}\in\mathrm{span}(e_0)$; if $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future
timelike this holds exactly when $P_{\mathrm{tot}}=\lambda e_0$ with
$\lambda>0$, and then $E_{e_0}(P_{\mathrm{tot}})=Mc^2$ for $M$ as in (b).

**(d) Comparison with the single-vector convention.** For a single future
timelike vector $P$, the invariant mass $M$ of (b) coincides with $m(P)$ of
[[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; in particular if
$P=mU$ with $m>0$ and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ (the four-velocity normalisation of
[[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), then $M=m$. Both quantities
are functions of the scalar $\eta(P,P)$ alone.

**(e) Scope.** This definition asserts no existence of a center-of-momentum
frame (that is [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]]), no physical conservation
law and no dynamics; only the total vector carries the invariant mass, and the
individual summands need not be causal for the sum to be defined. No choice
principle is used.

Throughout, $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ is the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski
model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], $c>0$, and $n\in V$ is future unit
timelike, $\eta(n,n)=-1$ ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]],
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]). Write
$n^\perp=\{v\in V:\eta(n,v)=0\}$ for the rest space of $n$,
$h(v):=v+\eta(n,v)n$ for the rest
projection and $|w|:=\sqrt{\eta(w,w)}$ for the norm on $n^\perp$
([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c)); recall from that
clause that $h$ is linear with image $n^\perp$ and kernel $\mathrm{span}(n)$,
that $V=\mathrm{span}(n)\oplus n^\perp$, and that the restriction of $\eta$ to
$n^\perp$ is positive definite.

**(a) Observer energy, spatial momentum and invariant mass.** For every $P$ in
the future closed cone $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ define

$$E_n(P):=-c\,\eta(P,n), \qquad q_n(P):=h(P),$$

and, when $P$ is nonzero future causal, define the **invariant mass** of $P$ by

$$m(P):=\frac{\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}}{c} .$$

Then $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$, $\eta(n,P)=-E_n(P)/c$, and

$$P=\frac{E_n(P)}{c}\,n+q_n(P)$$

is the unique decomposition of $P$ as a real multiple of $n$ plus a vector of
$n^\perp$: a vector $P$ has $P=\lambda n+w$ with $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and
$w\in n^\perp$ if and only if $\lambda=E_n(P)/c$ and $w=q_n(P)$. Equivalently,
$E_n(P)$ and $q_n(P)$ are the unique pair consisting of a real number and a
vector of $n^\perp$ with that property. The pair $(E_n,q_n)$ is the
restriction to $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ of the pair of linear maps
$P\mapsto -c\,\eta(P,n)$ and $P\mapsto h(P)$ on $V$. For future null $P$ the
formula for $m(P)$ gives $m(P)=0$, because $\eta(P,P)=0$.

**(b) Rest-mass parameter, rest energy and kinetic energy.** Let $m>0$ and let
$P=mU$ with $U$ future timelike and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, the four-velocity
normalisation of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]. Then call $m$
the **rest-mass parameter** of $P$ as written, $mc^2$ its **rest energy**, and

$$T_n(P):=E_n(P)-mc^2$$

its **kinetic energy** relative to the observer $n$. Bilinearity gives
$\eta(P,P)=m^2\eta(U,U)=-m^2c^2$, so $m=m(P)>0$ is determined by $P$.
Thus $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-m(P)c^2$ is a function of $(P,n)$ on the future
timelike cone; recording $m$ supplies no independent parameter.

**(c) No positivity, inequality or measurement claim.** This definition claims
no positivity of $E_n$, no inequality or vanishing property of $T_n$, and no
physical measurement. The names observer energy, spatial momentum, invariant
mass, rest energy and kinetic energy, and the units joule, kilogram metre per
second and kilogram, belong to the unit conventions of
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and to the physical postulates
of this framework; the mathematical content asserted here is only the explicit
dependence of the five quantities on $P$, $n$ and $m$.

**(d) What the objects depend on.** $E_n$ and $q_n$ are functions of the pair
$(P,n)$: $q_n(P)$ is an element of the vector space $V$, not a coordinate
triple, and no basis of $V$ enters its definition, while
$E_n(P)=-c\,\eta(P,n)$ uses the Lorentz form alone. $m(P)$ depends on the
scalar $\eta(P,P)$ alone and hence on no observer and no basis; $T_n(P)$
uses the rest mass $m=m(P)$ fixed by that scalar. No choice principle is
used.

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), with orientation fixed as a positive ray of
the determinant line $\Lambda^4V$
([[def-determinant-line-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space]])
and with the corresponding class of positively oriented ordered bases of $V$
([[def-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space]]); by
[[prop-orientations-and-positive-basis-classes-agree-in-positive-dimension]] the
positive ray selects exactly one such class for $\dim V=4>0$.

An **inertial frame** of the model is a tuple $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ consisting
of an event $o\in A$ and an ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $V$ that is

1. **$\eta$-orthonormal**: $\eta(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ for all $a,b$ ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]]);
2. **future**: $e_0\in C^+$, i.e. $e_0$ is future timelike; and
3. **positively oriented**: the ordered basis lies in the positive-basis class
   selected by the fixed orientation.

The event $o$ is the **origin** of the frame and $e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ are its
**basis vectors**.

**Inertial charts.** For an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, define

$$E:\mathbb R^4\longrightarrow V,\qquad E(u):=\sum_{a=0}^3u^ae_a .$$

Then $E$ is a linear isomorphism ([[def-linear-isomorphism-and-invertible-linear-map]]):
it is linear by construction, and it is bijective because
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is an ordered basis, every $v\in V$ having exactly one
coordinate list $u$ with $v=\sum_au^ae_a$
([[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]). The **inertial
chart** of the frame is the map

$$x:A\longrightarrow\mathbb R^4,\qquad x(p):=E^{-1}(p-o),$$

and its values $x^a(p)$ are the **inertial coordinates of the event $p$** in the
frame. Since $E$ and $v\mapsto p+v$ are bijections, $x$ is a bijection
$A\to\mathbb R^4$; and $x(p)=0$ exactly when $p-o=0_V$, that is, exactly when
$p=o$.

**Transition law.** Let $(o';e'_0,e'_1,e'_2,e'_3)$ be another inertial frame
with chart $x'$, and let $M=(M^b_a)$ be the change-of-basis matrix defined by
$e'_a=\sum_bM^b_ae_b$, a $4\times4$ real matrix that is invertible because both
families are ordered bases. Then $E'(u)=\sum_au^ae'_a=E(Mu)$ for all
$u\in\mathbb R^4$, for the matrix-vector product $Mu$ in the coordinates of the
first frame, because $\sum_au^a\sum_bM^b_ae_b=\sum_b(\sum_aM^b_au^a)e_b$; hence
$E'=E\circ M$ and $E'^{-1}=M^{-1}\circ E^{-1}$, so for every event $p$,

$$x'(p)=M^{-1}\bigl(x(p)-x(o')\bigr)=M^{-1}x(p)-M^{-1}x(o') .$$

In particular the transition between two inertial charts is an affine map of
$\mathbb R^4$ with invertible linear part $M^{-1}$ and constant part
$-M^{-1}x(o')$, and it is a bijection of $\mathbb R^4$ with inverse
$u\mapsto Mu+x(o')$, which is the transition in the reverse direction.

**The inertial atlas.** The **inertial atlas** of the model is the family of
all inertial frames together with their inertial charts. Its charts are
available at every event by [[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]], which
supplies for every $o\in A$ an inertial frame with origin $o$; and any two of
its charts are related by the affine transition displayed above.

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]) and use
the reachability objects $J^+$, $I^+$ of
[[def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space]]. Let
$(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with chart $x$
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) and let
$$|v_s|:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}$$
be the Euclidean norm of the spatial part $v_s:=v^1e_1+v^2e_2+v^3e_3$ of a
vector $v=v^0e_0+v_s$
([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]). Then:

**(a) Cone description.** $C^+=\{v:v^0>|v_s|\}$,
$\overline{C^+}=\{v:v^0\ge|v_s|\}$, $C^-=\{v:-v^0>|v_s|\}$ and
$\overline{C^-}=\{v:-v^0\ge|v_s|\}$; moreover every $v\in\overline{C^+}$ with
$v\ne 0$ satisfies $-\eta(v,e_0)=v^0>0$ and $|v_s|\le v^0$, and $v$ is future
null exactly when $|v_s|=v^0>0$.

**(b) Finite sums.** If $v_1,\dots,v_k$ lie in $\overline{C^+}$
($k\ge 1$), then $v_1+\cdots+v_k\in\overline{C^+}$; if in addition at least one
$v_i$ lies in $C^+$, then the sum lies in $C^+$; and if $v+w=0$ with
$v,w\in\overline{C^+}$, then $v=w=0$.

**(c) Coordinate criterion.** For events $p,q\in A$ put
$D^a:=x^a(q)-x^a(p)$ and $D_s:=(D^1,D^2,D^3)$. Then: $q\in J^+(p)$ if and only
if $D^0\ge|D_s|$; $q\in I^+(p)$ if and only if $D^0>|D_s|$; $q\in J^+(p)$ with
$q\ne p$ if and only if $D^0\ge|D_s|$ and $D^0>0$; and for $q\in J^+(p)$ with
$q\ne p$ one has $0<D^0$ and $|D_s|\le D^0$. The criteria are stated for the
chart of any inertial frame, because every inertial basis is
$\eta$-orthonormal with future first vector.

**(d) Scope.** The lemma is a statement about the affine model and the fixed
time orientation; it attaches no physical meaning to $\le$, $J^+$ or $I^+$ and
uses no choice principle.

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, and let $Q\in V$ be future
timelike with invariant mass $M:=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$
([[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]\,(b)); put
$n_Q:=Q/(Mc)$, so that $\eta(n_Q,n_Q)=-1$, $n_Q\in C^+$ and $Q=Mc\,n_Q$.

**(a)** There exists an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with $e_0=n_Q$;
in every such frame $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$, $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$ and the components of
$Q$ are $(Mc,0,0,0)$. Such a frame is a center-of-momentum frame of $Q$ in the
sense of [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]\,(c).

**(b)** Conversely, if an inertial frame satisfies $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$, then
$e_0=n_Q$. Hence the time vector of a center-of-momentum frame of $Q$ is
unique, and two center-of-momentum frames of $Q$ differ only by the choice of
origin and by a positively oriented $\eta$-orthonormal change of the spatial
basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $n_Q^\perp$; in particular the center-of-momentum
frame at a fixed origin is unique up to spatial rotations.

**(c)** If $Q$ is a nonzero future null vector, then no inertial frame
satisfies $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$: a nonzero future null vector has no
center-of-momentum frame.

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), $c>0$, let $n\in V$ be future unit
timelike, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and let $E_n,q_n,m,T_n$ be the quantities of
[[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]].

**(a)** If $P$ is nonzero future causal, then $E_n(P)>0$, $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$
and

$$\eta(q_n(P),q_n(P))=\frac{E_n(P)^2}{c^2}+\eta(P,P)\ \ge\ 0 .$$

Consequently: (i) if $P$ is future null, then $\eta(P,P)=0$ and
$E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$; (ii) if $P$ is future timelike with invariant mass
$m(P)$, then $\eta(P,P)=-m(P)^2c^2$ and the mass-shell identity

$$E_n(P)^2=m(P)^2c^4+c^2\,|q_n(P)|^2$$

holds. The invariant mass $m(P)$ depends only on the scalar $\eta(P,P)$ and
therefore on no observer $n$ and no basis, while $E_n$ and $q_n$ do depend on
$n$.

**(b)** Let $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant, let $U$ be future timelike with
$\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ (the four-velocity normalisation of
[[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), and put
$\gamma:=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$ and $w:=c\,h(U/c)/\gamma\in n^\perp$, the
relative velocity of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d)
applied to the future unit vector $u=U/c$; equivalently $w=h(U)/\gamma$. Then

$$E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma,\qquad T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)\ \ge\ 0,\qquad q_n(P)=m\gamma w,$$

and $m(P)=m$. Moreover $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if $\gamma=1$, that is $U=cn$,
equivalently $P=mcn$ (the particle is at rest relative to $n$). Finally
$|q_n(P)|=m\gamma|w|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}$.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $a_0, \dots, a_{n-1}$ and $b_0, \dots, b_{n-1}$ be
reals, with finite sums as in [[def-finite-sum]]. Then

$$\Big(\sum_{k<n} a_k b_k\Big)^{2} \;\le\; \Big(\sum_{k<n} a_k^{2}\Big)\Big(\sum_{k<n} b_k^{2}\Big),$$

and, in root form ([[thm-of-square-roots]]),

$$\Big|\sum_{k<n} a_k b_k\Big| \;\le\; \sqrt{\sum_{k<n} a_k^{2}} \; \sqrt{\sum_{k<n} b_k^{2}}.$$

Equality holds in the first display if and only if the two lists are
proportional, in the symmetric sense that there is a pair
$(\lambda, \mu) \ne (0,0)$ of reals with $\lambda a_k = \mu b_k$ for every
$k < n$.

**No root is used in the proof of the squared form.** That form is an identity
plus a sign argument in the ordered field, and the root form is only a
restatement of it through the monotonicity of squaring on the nonnegatives
([[lem-of-square-monotone]]); the root enters nowhere but the last step, where
that restatement is made and [[thm-of-square-roots]] is what supplies the
square-root symbol. This matters here, because it makes the squared
inequality independent of the existence theorem for roots.

derivations.claim: By [F3], applying the finite-sum cone rule to the nonzero future-causal $P_i$ shows that $Q$ is future causal. In the fixed inertial frame each nonzero future-causal summand has positive time component, so the time component of $Q$ is a finite sum of positive numbers and $Q\ne0$. If one summand is timelike, [F3] gives that $Q$ is future timelike.

Suppose every $P_i$ is null. Write its coordinates as $P_i=(a_i,u_i)$ in the fixed frame. By [F3], $a_i=|u_i|>0$. Then $Q$ is null exactly when $|\sum_i u_i|=\sum_i|u_i|$. Squaring both sides, this equality is equivalent to $\sum_{i<j}(|u_i||u_j|-u_i\cdot u_j)=0$. For each pair, apply [F6] to singleton coordinate lists to get $u_i\cdot u_j\le|u_i||u_j|$; therefore every summand is nonnegative. Equality of the sum forces equality for every pair, and equality with positive dot product forces each pair to be positively proportional. Thus all $P_i$ lie on one future null ray. Conversely, positive multiples of one future-null vector sum to a future-null vector. If the directions are not all the same, the inequality is strict, so the already future-causal $Q$ is timelike.

Let $Q$ be future timelike and use the center-of-momentum frame of [F4]. The total spatial momentum is zero and $E_{n_Q}(Q)=M(Q)c^2$. By linearity of $E_{n_Q}$, $M(Q)c^2=\sum_i E_{n_Q}(P_i)$. Each term satisfies $E_{n_Q}(P_i)\ge m_i c^2$ by the mass-shell identities in [F5], proving $M(Q)\ge\sum_i m_i$.

Equality in step 1.3 requires equality in every nonnegative term $E_{n_Q}(P_i)-m_i c^2$. A nonzero null $P_i$ has $m_i=0$ but $E_{n_Q}(P_i)>0$ by [F5], so equality excludes null legs. For a timelike leg, [F5] gives $E_{n_Q}(P_i)=m_i c^2$ exactly when $q_{n_Q}(P_i)=0$; then its observer decomposition is $P_i=(E_{n_Q}(P_i)/c)n_Q=m_i c n_Q$. Conversely, if every leg has the form $P_i=m_i c n$ with one common future unit timelike $n$, then $Q=c(\sum_i m_i)n$, so $M(Q)=\sum_i m_i$ directly.

For the relativistic-particle-mechanics collision configurations of [[def-rpm-collision-objects]], adopt the isolated-collision balance already stated in clause (iii) of [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]: when the event is isolated and the incoming and outgoing lists contain every leg, $Q_{\rm in}=Q_{\rm out}$. This local postulate records the exact collision interface used on this page; it is a scoped reuse of the existing adopted model assumption, not a second independent conservation assumption.

The balance is an adopted physical premise. It does not show that any specified reaction occurs and supplies no interaction mechanism, selection rule, probability, cross section, or amplitude. The cited treatments motivate and explain the model formulation; they do not turn the postulate into a deductive theorem or a report of an observed collision.

Use the flat oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski model, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and SI convention $x^0=ct$ of [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. A **relativistic-particle-mechanics collision configuration** is a mass-specified causal collision datum of [[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]]: an event $p\in A$, a finite nonempty incoming list $P_1,\ldots,P_N\in V$, and a finite nonempty outgoing list $P'_1,\ldots,P'_K\in V$, where every leg is a nonzero future-causal vector in the same displacement space $V$. A massive leg has a recorded mass $m>0$ and the massive-sector momentum of [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]]; a null leg has recorded mass $0$ and is a nonzero future-null vector with its scale specified independently. The definition does not identify a null momentum with $mU$ at $m=0$.

The side totals are the finite vector sums $Q_{\rm in}:=\sum_{i=1}^N P_i$ and $Q_{\rm out}:=\sum_{j=1}^K P'_j$. All legs are attached to the same event, so the sums compare vectors in one affine displacement space; no transport between different events is part of the datum. The adjective **isolated** is reserved for a model condition used by the postulate below: no external four-momentum transfer during the idealized event and no omitted incoming or outgoing leg.

At an event, an **observer** is a future unit timelike vector $n$ with $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and its rest space is $n^\perp=\{v\in V:\eta(v,n)=0\}$, as in [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. Observer energy $E_n(P):=-c\eta(P,n)$ and spatial momentum $q_n(P):=P+\eta(P,n)n\in n^\perp$ are those of [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]]. Their units are joules and kilogram metres per second. An inertial laboratory means one named inertial chart and its time-axis observer; it is not a general observer congruence or an arbitrary coordinate chart.

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model with $c>0$, and fix an inertial frame. For a finite nonempty list $P_1,\ldots,P_N$ of nonzero future-causal vectors in $V$, let $Q:=\sum_{i=1}^N P_i$, let $m_i:=\sqrt{-\eta(P_i,P_i)}/c$ (so $m_i=0$ exactly for a null leg), and let $M(Q)$ be the invariant mass of the total when $Q$ is timelike, as defined in [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]].

Then $Q$ is nonzero and future causal. If at least one $P_i$ is timelike, then $Q$ is future timelike. If all $P_i$ are null, then $Q$ is null exactly when all $P_i$ lie on the same future null ray; otherwise $Q$ is future timelike. Whenever $Q$ is timelike, the center-of-momentum frame exists, its time-axis observer $n_Q=Q/(M(Q)c)$ has zero total spatial momentum and total observer energy $M(Q)c^2$, and

$$M(Q)\ge\sum_{i=1}^N m_i.$$

Equality holds exactly when every $P_i$ is massive and there is one future unit timelike vector $n$ such that $P_i=m_i c\,n$ for every $i$. A nonzero future-null total has no center-of-momentum frame.

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, and let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^2$ future-timelike worldline in the flat Minkowski model of [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. Use one inertial frame and parameterize the curve by that chart's time coordinate $t$, so its coordinates are $(ct,\mathbf x(t))$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Identify the observer rest space with $\mathbb R^3$ by the frame's spatial orthonormal basis and use its Euclidean dot product and norm ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]). Write $\mathbf v=d\mathbf x/dt$, $\gamma=(1-|\mathbf v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, proper time $\tau$, and $U=dx/d\tau$. In the constant-mass sector of [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], let $m>0$ be constant and $P=mU$. In this chart write $P=(E/c,\mathbf p)$, where $E$ and $\mathbf p$ are the observer energy and spatial momentum of [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]]. Then $|\mathbf v|<c$, $E=\gamma mc^2>0$, $\mathbf p=\gamma m\mathbf v$, and

$$E^2=m^2c^4+c^2|\mathbf p|^2,\qquad \mathbf v=\frac{c^2\mathbf p}{E}.$$

Define the three-force by $\mathbf F:=d\mathbf p/dt$ and the four-force by $K:=dP/d\tau$ in this flat inertial chart. In SI units $m$ is in kilograms, $c$ and $\mathbf v$ in metres per second, $E$ in joules, $\mathbf p$ in kilogram metres per second, and $\mathbf F,K$ in newtons. Then

$$\frac{dE}{dt}=\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf v,\qquad K=\gamma\left(\frac{\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf v}{c},\mathbf F\right).$$

Separately, let $I_\tau\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open proper-time interval, let $m:I_\tau\to(0,\infty)$ be $C^1$, and let $U:I_\tau\to V$ be a $C^1$ future timelike vector field with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Measure $m$ in kilograms and $dm/d\tau$ in kilograms per second, and set $P(\tau):=m(\tau)U(\tau)$. With $K:=dP/d\tau$, the kinematic ansatz satisfies

$$\eta(P,K)=-m\,\frac{dm}{d\tau}\,c^2.$$

The last identity is only a differentiated mass-shell relation; it prescribes no evolution for $m$. None of these conclusions assumes a force law.

Throughout, $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ is the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski
model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and $c>0$.

**(a) Total four-momentum.** For a finite list $(P_1,\dots,P_N)$, $N\ge0$, of
vectors of $V$, define the **total four-momentum**
$P_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\sum_{i=1}^{N}P_i$ as the finite sum of
[[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]] in the additive group $(V,+)$ of
the vector space $V$; the empty sum is $0$. The sum uses the vectors $P_i$
alone: no event, no position and no simultaneity datum enters it, and the
order of the list does not affect $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ because addition in $V$
is commutative.

**(b) Invariant mass of the total.** If $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future timelike
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]), define the **invariant
mass** of the system and its **rest energy** by

This local postulate records the exact collision interface used on this page; it is a scoped reuse of the existing adopted model assumption, not a second independent conservation assumption.

The balance is an adopted physical premise. It does not show that any specified reaction occurs and supplies no interaction mechanism, selection rule, probability, cross section, or amplitude. The cited treatments motivate and explain the model formulation; they do not turn the postulate into a deductive theorem or a report of an observed collision.

Use the flat oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski model, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and SI convention $x^0=ct$ of [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. A **relativistic-particle-mechanics collision configuration** is a mass-specified causal collision datum of [[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]]: an event $p\in A$, a finite nonempty incoming list $P_1,\ldots,P_N\in V$, and a finite nonempty outgoing list $P'_1,\ldots,P'_K\in V$, where every leg is a nonzero future-causal vector in the same displacement space $V$. A massive leg has a recorded mass $m>0$ and the massive-sector momentum of [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]]; a null leg has recorded mass $0$ and is a nonzero future-null vector with its scale specified independently. The definition does not identify a null momentum with $mU$ at $m=0$.

The side totals are the finite vector sums $Q_{\rm in}:=\sum_{i=1}^N P_i$ and $Q_{\rm out}:=\sum_{j=1}^K P'_j$. All legs are attached to the same event, so the sums compare vectors in one affine displacement space; no transport between different events is part of the datum. At an event, an **observer** is a future unit timelike vector $n$ with $\eta(n,n)=-1$, and its rest space is $n^\perp=\{v\in V:\eta(v,n)=0\}$, as in [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. Their units are joules and kilogram metres per second. An inertial laboratory means one named inertial chart and its time-axis observer; it is not a general observer congruence or an arbitrary coordinate chart.

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, and let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^2$ future-timelike worldline in the flat Minkowski model of [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. Use one inertial frame and parameterize the curve by that chart's time coordinate $t$, so its coordinates are $(ct,\mathbf x(t))$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Identify the observer rest space with $\mathbb R^3$ by the frame's spatial orthonormal basis and use its Euclidean dot product and norm ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]). $$E^2=m^2c^4+c^2|\mathbf p|^2,\qquad \mathbf v=\frac{c^2\mathbf p}{E}.$$

$$\frac{dE}{dt}=\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf v,\qquad K=\gamma\left(\frac{\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf v}{c},\mathbf F\right).$$

$$\eta(P,K)=-m\,\frac{dm}{d\tau}\,c^2.$$

Use the massive and null sectors as separately adopted in [[post-rpm-massive-test-particle-action]] and [[post-rpm-null-test-particle-action]]. For a massive body of constant mass $m>0$, its **mechanical four-momentum** is $P=mU$, where along an admissible $C^2$ future timelike trajectory $x:I\to M$, with $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval with nonempty interior and parameter $s$, put $T=dx/ds$, and $U:=cT/\sqrt{-g(T,T)}$ is its future tangent normalized by $g(U,U)=-c^2$. The clock convention in the massive-sector adoption gives $d\tau/ds=\sqrt{-g(T,T)}/c$, so $U=dx/d\tau$. $$q_n(P):=P+g(P,n)n\in n^\perp,\qquad E_n(P):=-c\,g(P,n).$$
